$comment: Generated by scripts/preprocess-planets.sh (scripts/planets). Do not edit by hand.

uv.projection: equirectangular (plate carree), 2:1, pixel-is-area: texel (i, k) covers longitudes [i, i + 1] * 360 / W and latitudes from the south pole up
uv.u: u = (uAtLon0 + lon / 360) mod 1 for lonIncreases 'right' (east longitude lon in degrees); u = 0 and u = 1 are the same meridian
uv.v: v = 0.5 + lat / 180: v = 0 is the south pole, v = 1 the north pole (lat in the body's latitude convention)
uv.rowOrder: bottom-up: the first stored row of every mip level is the southernmost. The files carry KTXorientation 'ru' to say so. three's KTX2Loader never flips KTX2 (flipY stays false), so uv.y = 0 samples the first stored row: use the textures as loaded
uv.sampler: wrapS = RepeatWrapping, wrapT = ClampToEdgeWrapping, minFilter = LinearMipmapLinearFilter, magFilter = LinearFilter. Raw R8 and RGBA8 files load as DataTexture with nearest filtering and no wrap: set these explicitly. Sample with seam-safe gradients (as src/chapters/ch02/cmb-sphere.ts does) so the u = 0/1 seam picks the right mip level
uv.mipChain: every level to 1 x 1, made by scripts/planets: Lanczos-2 in linear light, wrapping in longitude and clamped at the poles (box filter for the water mask and the ring strip)

earth.longitude: east longitude (Greenwich at u = 0.5), as in the source maps (-180 to 180 from the left edge)
earth.latitude: geodetic (WGS 84), i.e. the latitude of the surface normal
earth.caption: A composite of several epochs: land and sea ice July 2004, clouds 2001, night lights 2016.

day.description: Daytime surface colour (land, ice and ocean, July 2004), no relief shading baked in.

night.description: City lights at night (2016), the faint land floor removed. Present-day Earth only.

channels.r: R8, sRGB-encoded brightness (decode with the sRGB curve before adding as emission).

clouds.description: Cloud cover (2001 composite; the poles from thermal infrared, so Antarctica reads as cloud).

water.description: Water mask for ocean specular and flat water: oceans, seas and lakes.

channels.r: R8, water fraction 0..1 (1 = water), from 4 x 4 supersampled vectors.

normal.description: Land relief as tangent-space normals from ETOPO 2022 surface heights (ice surface on ice sheets); water is flat.

channels.x: east slope component, in r (and g, b): UASTC normal mode stores X in RGB and Y in alpha
channels.decode: n.xy = texel.ga * 2 - 1 (or .ra); tangent frame at the surface point: x toward local east (increasing u), y toward local north (increasing v), z outward

moon.longitude: east longitude (mean Earth / polar axis frame, centre of the near side at u = 0.5)
moon.latitude: planetocentric (the Moon is a sphere here)
moon.caption: LROC colour and LOLA relief.

colour.description: Natural-colour albedo (LROC WAC, Hapke-normalised: no shading baked in).

normal.description: LOLA relief as tangent-space normals (source 16 pixels per degree, so 4096 is the widest level).

channels.x: east slope component, in r (and g, b): UASTC normal mode stores X in RGB and Y in alpha
channels.decode: n.xy = texel.ga * 2 - 1 (or .ra); tangent frame at the surface point: x toward local east (increasing u), y toward local north (increasing v), z outward

jupiter.longitude: System III east longitude E = 360 - W from u = 0: the OPAL map's left edge is 0 degrees west and west longitude decreases to the right
jupiter.latitude: planetographic (sample with the latitude of the ellipsoid's outward normal); OPAL navigated with radii 71492 / 66854 km
jupiter.caption: Hubble OPAL, 2025-12-11. The Great Red Spot drifts in longitude; its position here is that date's.

colour.description: Hubble OPAL colour composite of 2025-12-11 (source 3600 x 1800, so 4096 is the widest level).

saturn.longitude: System III east longitude E = 360 - W from u = 0 (the OPAL map's left edge is 360 degrees west, decreasing to the right)
saturn.latitude: planetographic (sample with the latitude of the ellipsoid's outward normal); OPAL navigated with radii 60268 / 54364 km
saturn.caption: Hubble OPAL, 2025-08-29, near the ring-plane crossing.

colour.description: Hubble OPAL colour composite of 2025-08-29 (source 1800 x 900, so 2048 is the widest level).

rings.description: Saturn's main rings along their radius: opacity from the Cassini RSS normal optical depth (2005), colour of the lit face from the Cassini PIA11142 mosaic (2008). One 8192 x 1 strip for every tier.

channels.a: normal opacity 1 - exp(-tau), tau the RSS normal optical depth averaged as transmission over the texel, and 0 where tau is below the profile's noise floor (facts.saturnRings.opacityNoise); for a ray at angle mu = |cos| to the ring normal use 1 - (1 - a)^(1/mu)
channels.rgb: straight alpha (not premultiplied): the colour of the ring material's lit face, the PIA11142 colour divided by the share of a thick ring's light the ring returned in that mosaic's geometry (facts.saturnRings.colourModel), so thin rings are not darkened twice. Gaps and the empty space inside the C ring and beyond the A ring carry the nearest ring material's colour, so filtering never pulls black into the rings. Blend as mix(background, rgb * light, a_view) with a_view = 1 - (1 - a)^(1/mu)

greatRedSpot.method: centre of the reddest 3-degree patch (red minus blue) within 60 degrees of the equator

saturnRings.u: u = (r - radiusKm[0]) / (radiusKm[1] - radiusKm[0]); texel i covers that span's i-th 1/8192

colourRegistration.method: 17 rows averaged along the arcs' apex; column to radius piecewise linear through ring edges and gaps found in both the image and the RSS opacity; the Keeler Gap checks it

colourModel.method: single scattering: a ring of normal optical depth tau returns 1 - exp(-tau * pathFactor) of a thick ring's light, pathFactor = 1/sin(viewElevation) + 1/sin(|sunElevation|) for the mosaic; its colour is divided by that share where the share is at least minShare and the mosaic is not black within edgeMarginTexels, and every other texel takes the nearest such texel's colour
colourModel.sunElevationFrom: Saturn's position from public/assets/jpl/planets.json, its pole from physical.json

observation.opacity: Cassini RSS X-band occultation, Rev 7 egress, 2005-05-03, ring opening -23.57 degrees
observation.colour: Cassini ISS PIA11142, 2008-11-26, lit face from 10 degrees below, 28 degrees phase
